title: Reading aloud
text: Your teacher asks you to read a page aloud in front of the class. Your tummy feels fluttery and your hands are a little shaky. What do you do?
options: a) Notice I'm nervous, take a slow breath, and start reading | b) Say I feel sick so I don't have to read | c) Quietly tell the teacher I'm nervous | d) Read super fast to get it over with

title: A grumpy morning
text: You've been grumpy all morning. When your little sister asks to borrow a pencil, you snap at her and she walks away upset. You're not even sure why you feel this way. What do you do?
options: a) Think about what's bothering me. Maybe I'm worried about today's test | b) Ignore it. It's her fault for bothering me | c) Say sorry to my sister and tell her I'm in a bad mood | d) Put on headphones and avoid everyone

title: The knocked-over tower
text: You spent all break building a tall block tower. Arjun walks past, knocks it over on purpose, and laughs. Your face feels hot and you want to shout. What do you do?
options: a) Shout at Arjun and knock over his things | b) Count to five, breathe, then tell him that wasn't okay | c) Tell a teacher what happened | d) Walk away and keep it all inside

title: The dropped catch
text: It's the last over of the inter-house cricket match. The ball flies straight to you, and you drop it. Your team loses by two runs, and a few teammates groan loudly. What do you do?
options: a) Blame the sun in my eyes | b) Feel bad for a while, then tell the team I'll practise my catching | c) Quit the team so it never happens again | d) Pretend I don't care and laugh it off

title: The night before results
text: Exam results come out tomorrow. It's late, but you can't sleep. Your mind keeps imagining bad marks and what your parents might say. What do you do?
options: a) Scroll on my phone for hours to distract myself | b) Tell a parent I'm worried about tomorrow | c) Write down my worries and take slow breaths | d) Decide I've definitely failed and get upset

title: Lunch alone
text: A new girl, Meher, joined your class this week. Every lunch break she sits alone and stares at her tiffin. Your friends are waving you over to their table. What do you do?
options: a) Go and sit with my friends like always | b) Ask Meher if she'd like to join us | c) Ask my friends to invite her over

title: A quiet friend
text: Your best friend Kabir usually talks non-stop. Today he's quiet, isn't joining the game, and keeps looking at the ground. What do you do?
options: a) Leave him alone and keep playing | b) Sit with him and ask if he's okay | c) Tell him to stop being boring and come play | d) Make a silly face to cheer him up

title: One swing, two friends
text: There's only one free swing, and you and your friend Zoya reach it at the same time. You both really want it. What do you do?
options: a) Grab it. I was here first | b) Take turns, counting 20 swings each | c) Let Zoya have it and walk away sad | d) Play rock-paper-scissors to decide who goes first

title: The group project
text: Your science project is due on Monday. Your partner Rohan hasn't done any of his part and keeps saying, "I'll do it later." You're getting worried. What do you do?
options: a) Do his part myself without saying anything | b) Talk to Rohan and agree who does what by Saturday | c) Complain about him to the whole class | d) Tell the teacher Rohan isn't helping

title: Lost in maths class
text: Your teacher explains a new kind of sum. Everyone else seems to understand, but you're completely lost. The teacher asks, "Any questions?" What do you do?
options: a) Stay quiet so nobody thinks I'm silly | b) Put my hand up and ask | c) Ask the teacher after class | d) Copy a friend's answers later

title: Words that hurt
text: Yesterday, when your best friend Ananya forgot to save you a seat, you called her "useless" in front of others. Today she's sitting with someone else and won't look at you. What do you do?
options: a) Wait for her to talk to me first | b) Say sorry and explain I was upset, not angry at her | c) Make fun of her new friend | d) Write her a note to say sorry

title: The broken vase
text: While playing ball indoors, you knock your grandmother's favourite vase off the shelf. It breaks. Nobody saw it happen. What do you do?
options: a) Hide the pieces and say nothing | b) Tell Dadi what happened and say sorry | c) Say the cat knocked it over

title: The dare
text: Your friends plan to skip the last class and go to the shop. They dare you to come: "Don't be a baby, nobody will notice." You don't want to get into trouble, but you don't want to look scared either. What do you do?
options: a) Go with them so they don't laugh at me | b) Say no and stay for class | c) Suggest we go to the shop together after school instead | d) Pretend I'm sick so I have an excuse

title: The group chat photo
text: Someone posts an embarrassing photo of a classmate, Tara, in your class group chat. People are adding laughing emojis. Tara is in the group too. What do you do?
options: a) Add a laughing emoji like everyone else | b) Message the person privately and ask them to delete it | c) Tell a teacher or parent about it | d) Send Tara a kind message

title: Left out of the game
text: For three days, a group of kids hasn't let you join their game. Today one of them said, "There's no space for you." You feel lonely and sad. What do you do?
options: a) Tell a teacher or someone at home how I feel | b) Look for someone else who's playing alone | c) Decide nobody likes me and stop trying | d) Say something mean back to them

title: Not picked
text: You've practised basketball every evening for weeks. Today the coach announced the team, and your name wasn't on the list. Your best friend made it. What do you do?
options: a) Ask the coach what I can work on for next time | b) Tell myself I'm bad at everything | c) Congratulate my friend, even though I feel sad | d) Ignore my friend because I'm jealous

title: Sharing sweets fairly
text: You have 12 sweets and 4 friends at your birthday party. You want everyone to get the same number. How many sweets does each friend get?
options: a) 2 | b) 3 [answer] | c) 4 | d) 6

title: Saving for a book
text: Aarav has ₹45. The storybook he wants costs ₹70. If he saves ₹5 every day, how many days until he can buy it?
options: a) 4 days | b) 5 days [answer] | c) 6 days | d) 25 days

title: When does lunch end?
text: Lunch break starts at 12:40 and lasts 35 minutes. What time does lunch break end?

title: Vans for the class trip
text: 38 students are going on a class trip. Each van holds 8 students. How many vans are needed so nobody is left behind?

title: Festival sale
text: A pair of shoes costs ₹800. The shop has a 25% off sale for the festival. What is the sale price?

title: Meera's next test
text: Meera scored 72, 85 and 90 in three tests. What does she need in the fourth test to have an average of 85?

title: What comes next?
text: Look at the numbers: 2, 4, 8, 16, … What number comes next?

title: The lunch queue
text: In the lunch queue, Riya is in front of Kabir. Kabir is in front of Sam. Who is at the back of the queue?
options: a) Riya | b) Kabir | c) Sam [answer]

title: Odd one out
text: Which one does not belong with the others: apple, mango, carrot, banana?
options: a) Apple | b) Mango | c) Carrot [answer] | d) Banana

title: The last laddoo
text: Someone ate the last laddoo. Anu says, "Bilal ate it." Bilal says, "I didn't eat it." Chitra says, "I didn't eat it." Only one of them is telling the truth. Who ate the laddoo?
options: a) Anu | b) Bilal | c) Chitra [answer]

title: Square numbers
text: What comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, …?

title: Which day was it?
text: If the day after tomorrow is Sunday, what day was yesterday?
options: a) Wednesday | b) Thursday [answer] | c) Friday | d) Saturday

title: Feeling anxious
text: Kabir felt anxious before the school race. What does anxious mean?
options: a) Worried or nervous [answer] | b) Very happy | c) Sleepy | d) Angry

title: Opposite of generous
text: Priya is generous. She always shares her colours. What is the opposite of generous?
options: a) Kind | b) Selfish [answer] | c) Rich | d) Brave

title: Another word for brave
text: Zoya was brave when she spoke up for a new student. Which word means the same as brave?
options: a) Scared | b) Courageous [answer] | c) Quiet | d) Tired

title: Feeling frustrated
text: Ira felt frustrated when her science model kept falling apart. What does frustrated mean here?
options: a) Annoyed because things weren't working [answer] | b) Excited about something new | c) Tired after a long day | d) Proud of her work

title: What is empathy?
text: Your teacher says, "Arjun showed real empathy today." Which sentence best describes empathy?
options: a) Understanding how someone else feels [answer] | b) Being the best at a game | c) Following every rule | d) Speaking very loudly

title: A gracious loser
text: After losing the cricket match, Dev stayed ______ and congratulated the other team. Which word fits best?
options: a) gracious [answer] | b) furious | c) careless | d) boastful

title: Smiling on the outside
text: Your cousin Riya wins the drawing prize you really hoped for. Everyone claps, and you smile too, but inside you feel heavy. That evening Nani asks how your day was. What do you do?
options: a) Say "Fine!" and quickly change the topic | b) Tell her you're happy for Riya, but a bit disappointed too | c) Say the competition was unfair | d) Go to your room and start a new drawing

title: Tight fists at the park
text: At the park, a boy keeps cutting in front of you at the slide. You notice your fists are tight and your face feels hot. What do you do?
options: a) Notice I'm getting angry and take a few slow breaths first | b) Push him off the ladder | c) Tell him clearly, "It's my turn now" | d) Pretend I don't mind and go home

title: Rain on sports day
text: Sports day is cancelled because of heavy rain. You practised your race every evening this week. What do you do?
options: a) Sulk and refuse to join anything today | b) Ask the teacher if the race can happen another day | c) Tell myself my practice still counts, then join the indoor games | d) Blame my friend for saying it wouldn't rain

title: Laddoos for the guests
text: Ammi made laddoos for the guests coming tonight and asked you not to touch them. You are alone in the kitchen and very hungry. What do you do?
options: a) Eat one. She won't notice | b) Ask Ammi for a snack I can have now | c) Go and play outside so I stop thinking about them | d) Eat one, then tell Ammi straight away

title: Juice on my shirt
text: In the lunch line, Farhan bumps into you and your juice spills all over your shirt. You didn't see whether he meant to do it. What do you do?
options: a) Shove him back | b) Ask, "Did you trip?" before deciding | c) Decide he did it on purpose and tell everyone | d) Say nothing but stay angry all day

title: The zoo trip
text: Your class trip is to the zoo, and you are thrilled. Your friend Arjun is quiet. He had hoped the trip would be to the science museum. What do you do?
options: a) Tell him the zoo is way better anyway | b) Ask him what he was hoping to see at the museum | c) Ignore it. It's a fun day | d) Ask the teacher if the museum could be a trip later

title: Quiet reading time
text: Ms. Iyer has said, "No talking during reading time." Your friend Kabir whispers that he feels sick and dizzy. What do you do?
options: a) Ignore him because it's quiet time | b) Raise my hand and tell Ms. Iyer that Kabir feels sick | c) Whisper, "Shh, we'll get in trouble" | d) Whisper, "Let's tell Ms. Iyer. I'll come with you"

title: The note under the desk
text: You find a fifty-rupee note under a desk in your classroom. Nobody saw you pick it up. What do you do?
options: a) Keep it | b) Give it to the class teacher | c) Ask around to find out who lost it | d) Buy sweets for everyone with it

title: Chotu wants to play
text: You and your friends are playing carrom. Your little brother Chotu wants to join, but he keeps knocking the pieces off the board. Dadi says, "Let him play too." What do you do?
options: a) Tell him to go away | b) Give him an important job, like keeping the score | c) Stop playing so nobody gets in trouble | d) Let him take my turn this round

title: First day at tuition
text: It's your first day at a new tuition class. Everyone already seems to know each other. Your tummy feels tight. What do you do?
options: a) Tell myself "I'm nervous, and that's okay" and say hi to someone | b) Say I feel sick so I can go home | c) Watch quietly first, then join a group at break | d) Act bored and don't talk to anyone

title: Two friends, two stories
text: Your two best friends, Ishaan and Rohan, have had a big fight. Each one wants you on his side and says the other is lying about what happened. What do you do?
options: a) Pick Ishaan. I've known him longer | b) Listen to each of them, say I won't take sides, and offer to help them talk | c) Avoid both of them until it blows over | d) Tell each of them what the other said about him

title: Seen, no reply
text: You messaged your friend Ananya about weekend plans. The chat shows she saw it two hours ago, but she hasn't replied. What do you do?
options: a) Assume she's ignoring me and send "fine, whatever" | b) Think of reasons she might be busy, and wait until tomorrow | c) Post a status about fake friends | d) Send a friendly "No worries if you're busy!"

title: Who cares about marks?
text: Neha usually tops maths. When she gets her test back, she laughs and says, "Who cares about marks!" Later, you notice her eyes are red. What do you do?
options: a) Joke, "You still did better than me!" | b) Quietly ask if she's okay, without pushing | c) Leave it. She said she doesn't care | d) Tell others that she was crying

title: Feeling down for days
text: For several days, your friend Sana has seemed low. She skips the games she used to love and says she's just tired. What do you do?
options: a) Tell her to cheer up | b) Ask how she is really doing, and listen | c) Suggest she talks to a grown-up she trusts, and offer to go with her | d) Tell the class that Sana is sad

title: A new classmate
text: Kiran, a new classmate, wears a hearing aid and sometimes asks people to repeat things. A few boys start mumbling on purpose when he asks. What do you do?
options: a) Laugh along with them | b) Face Kiran when I talk and ask what helps him | c) Tell the boys calmly, "That's not funny" | d) Tell the class teacher what's happening

title: That thought again
text: You score much lower than you expected on a science practice paper. One thought keeps repeating: "I'm just bad at science." What do you do?
options: a) Believe it and stop trying in science | b) Notice the thought, then check which topics I actually missed | c) Tell my teacher which chapters confused me | d) Hide the paper from everyone

title: Moving to Pune
text: Your family is moving to Pune for your mother's new job. You are excited about the new city, but sad to leave your friends. What do you do?
options: a) Tell my friends I feel both excited and sad | b) Act as if I'm only happy | c) Refuse to talk about it | d) Plan a video call with my best friend every Sunday

title: Whose idea was it?
text: In your group presentation, Tanvi presents your idea as her own, and the teacher praises her for it. What do you do?
options: a) Stand up and call her a liar in front of the class | b) Later, tell Tanvi calmly that it hurt and ask that we share the credit | c) Say nothing, but stop helping the group | d) Tell the teacher privately where the idea came from

title: A stranger in the game chat
text: Someone you don't know sends you a friend request in an online game. They say they're 13 too, and ask which school you go to. What do you do?
options: a) Tell them my school. They seem nice | b) Don't share anything, and tell a parent or trusted adult | c) Keep chatting, but give a made-up school name | d) Block them

title: The leaked answers
text: The night before a test, a classmate shares a photo of the answers in the class group chat. What do you do?
options: a) Look at it and memorise the answers | b) Don't open it, and tell the teacher the paper has leaked | c) Don't open it, but say nothing | d) Forward it so everyone has the same chance

title: The final or the function?
text: Your team's final cricket match is on the same evening as your cousin's engagement function. Your family is counting on you being there. What do you do?
options: a) Skip the function without telling anyone | b) Ask my parents if I can play the first half and come after | c) Go to the function and ask a teammate to take my place | d) Go to the function but sulk all evening

title: Three deadlines
text: This week you have a science project, a Hindi test and a dance rehearsal. Everything feels like too much at once. What do you do?
options: a) Make a list and plan a little for each day | b) Ask my teacher if the project deadline could move | c) Stay up very late every night to do everything | d) Avoid it all and watch videos

title: The red crayon
text: You and Meera both want the red crayon. You get it first. Meera looks sad. She wanted to colour a red apple. What do you do?
options: a) Use it quickly, then give it to Meera | b) Keep it. I got it first | c) Hide the crayon in my bag

title: The wet drawing
text: Kabir walks past your desk. Your water bottle falls and wets your drawing. Kabir stops and looks at the puddle. Did he mean it? What do you do?
options: a) Ask, "Was that an accident?" | b) Shout at Kabir and push him | c) Wipe it and stay quiet all day

title: Hot face at the swings
text: You were waiting for the swing. Riya runs and takes it first. Your face feels hot. Your hands make fists. What do you do?
options: a) Take three big, slow breaths | b) Pull Riya off the swing | c) Run off and hide

title: Ice cream after dinner
text: Papa bought ice cream. He says, "We will eat it after dinner." The freezer is right there. Papa is busy on the phone. What do you do?
options: a) Go and draw until dinner | b) Eat a big spoon now, quietly | c) Ask Papa, "Can I have some now?"

title: The broken cup
text: You are playing ball inside. The ball hits Mummy's cup and it breaks. Nobody saw. Mummy calls, "What was that noise?" What do you do?
options: a) Say, "It was me. I'm sorry." | b) Say, "The cat did it!" | c) Hide the pieces under the sofa

title: Alone at lunch
text: Tenzin is new. He speaks only a little Hindi. He sits alone at lunch. Your friends say, "Don't sit with him." What do you do?
options: a) Tell my friends, "Tenzin can sit with us!" | b) Do what my friends say | c) Tell the teacher Tenzin is alone

title: Lost at the market
text: You are at the market with Papa. You stop to look at balloons. Now you cannot see Papa! What do you do?
options: a) Stay here and ask the shopkeeper | b) Run around looking for Papa | c) Walk home by myself

title: One tablet, two children
text: There is one tablet. You and your little sister Diya both want to play now. What do you do?
options: a) Set a timer and take turns | b) Grab it and play first | c) Give it to her and be sad.

title: Quiet in the library
text: In the library, everyone must be quiet. Your friend Anjali trips and hurts her knee. She is crying. What do you do?
options: a) Stay quiet. That is the rule | b) Go and tell the teacher quickly | c) Laugh because she fell

title: "I don't care"
text: Ishaan is not picked for the race. He says, "I don't care." But his eyes look wet, and he looks at the ground. What do you do?
options: a) Sit with him and ask, "Are you sad?" | b) Say, "Okay!" and run to the race | c) Say, "Don't cry. It's only a race."

title: A message in the game
text: You are playing a game on Mummy's phone. A message pops up: "Hi! What is your name and school?" You don't know who it is. What do you do?
options: a) Show Mummy the message | b) Type my name and school | c) Close the game and say nothing

title: My tower, my turn
text: You are building a tower with blocks. Bunty keeps taking your blocks for his car. What do you do?
options: a) Say, "Please stop. I need those blocks." | b) Knock his car over | c) Let him take them all

title: Ro's balloons
text: Ro has 3 balloons. Kiki gives him 2 more. How many balloons does Ro have now?
options: a) 4 | b) 5 [answer] | c) 6

title: Mangoes in the basket
text: There are 7 mangoes in a basket. Meera eats 2. How many mangoes are left?
options: a) 4 | b) 5 [answer] | c) 9

title: Kiki's bead necklace
text: Kiki makes a necklace: red bead, blue bead, red bead, blue bead, red bead. Which colour comes next?
options: a) Red | b) Blue [answer] | c) Green

title: Big and small
text: The elephant is big. The mouse is the opposite of big. What is the mouse?
options: a) Small [answer] | b) Grey | c) Loud

title: Team jersey printing
text: Aditi and her 4 teammates want matching jerseys for the inter-school kho-kho tournament. The printer charges a flat ₹150 design fee plus ₹120 per jersey. If all 5 players share the total bill equally, how much should each player contribute?

title: Splitting the project bill
text: In the science group chat, Sana texts Mohit and the team: 'The poster boards and paints cost ₹360, plus ₹40 for delivery. Luckily, I found a coupon that takes ₹50 off our total bill! If the 5 of us split the remaining cost equally, how much should each person pay?'

title: Cones for the pitch
text: Karthik brings 8 plastic cones to mark the cricket pitch in the playground. Abdul brings 6 more cones. How many cones do they have altogether?

title: Pebbles in the Park
text: Nikhil collects 20 smooth pebbles in the neighbourhood park. He gives 4 pebbles to Ravi. Then, Nikhil divides the rest equally between his 2 jacket pockets. How many pebbles are in each pocket?
options: a) 6 | b) 8 [answer] | c) 10 | d) 16

title: Juice on the trip
text: During a rest stop on their school trip, Thomas and Diya offer to buy juice for their six-member group. A pack of 6 bottles costs ₹150, but the shopkeeper gives a school discount of ₹30. If all 6 friends split the final bill equally, how much does each person need to contribute?

title: Drill on the Track
text: During football conditioning, Coach asks Gurpreet to complete 4 sets of shuttle sprints. Each set covers 100 metres. Gurpreet runs at a steady pace of 5 metres per second. Coach insists on a 30-second breather between sets, but no break is needed after the final set ends. How many total seconds will Gurpreet need to finish the entire drill?

title: Paper Stars for the Wall
text: Ishita and Harsh are folding paper stars to decorate the living room. Ishita folds 5 stars every hour, and Harsh folds 4 stars every hour. Working together, how many hours will it take them to make 45 stars?
options: a) 4 hours | b) 5 hours [answer] | c) 9 hours | d) 10 hours

title: Boundary Markers
text: Lakshmi and Arnav are setting up cones along the 200-metre sprint track in the school playground for sports day. They place a cone right at the start line, and then one cone every 8 metres all the way to the finish line. How many cones do they place in total?

title: Sketch pens in the chat
text: In the class group chat, Irfan writes that their project team needs 20 sketch pens. They already have 8 pens in their kit. If 3 classmates bring the rest equally, how many pens should each classmate bring?
options: a) 3 | b) 4 [answer] | c) 6 | d) 12

title: Packing the Cookies
text: Vikram and Kavya bake 30 cookies at home. Vikram eats 2 warm cookies, and Kavya eats 4. They pack the rest equally into 4 gift boxes for their cousins. How many cookies go into each box?
options: a) 5 | b) 6 [answer] | c) 7 | d) 8

title: The Quest Door Keys
text: Aarav and Ishita need three keys to unlock an online game gate: Blue, Green, and Gold. The Blue key goes in before the Green key. The Gold key goes in before the Blue key. Which key must they use first?
options: a) Blue key | b) Green key | c) Gold key [answer]

title: The Carrom Clue
text:
At their cousin's house, Kavya posts a riddle in the cousins' group chat to find the carrom board:

'It is kept in either the study, the veranda, or the storeroom. It is on the ground floor, but not in any room that has a fan.'

Karthik checks the rooms:
• The study is upstairs.
• The veranda has a ceiling fan.

Where did Kavya put the carrom board?
options: a) The study | b) The veranda | c) The storeroom [answer]

title: The Photo Stool
text: At the wedding photobooth, Ishita wears a red dupatta. Vikram wears a blue kurta. Arnav wears a green jacket. The cousin standing on the wooden stool wears a green jacket. Who is on the stool?
options: a) Vikram | b) Arnav [answer] | c) Ishita

title: Sprint Timings
text: At sprint practice, four runners timed their laps. Divya wore blue and Mehul wore red; the other two runners wore green and yellow. Looking at the coach's board: Divya finished ahead of Mehul. Mehul did not finish last. The runner in third place wore green. Who finished in second place?
options: a) Divya | b) Mehul [answer] | c) The runner in green | d) The runner in yellow

title: Bibs for Practice
text: At sports practice, Divya and Uday pick bibs from a box. The box has three colours: green, orange, and blue. Uday takes the blue bib. Divya does not want the orange bib. Which bib does Divya choose?
options: a) Green [answer] | b) Orange | c) Blue

title: Flashlight lineup in the dark
text:
During a sudden power cut at home, Karthik and Ravi line up four flashlights in a row on the table from left to right: Amber, Blue, Green, and Red.

• The Red flashlight is at an outer end, but not the far right.
• The Amber flashlight is placed directly between Red and Blue.
• The Blue flashlight sits to the left of the Green flashlight.

Which flashlight is in the third position from the left?
options: a) Amber | b) Blue [answer] | c) Green | d) Red

title: Slippers by the Door
text: At his cousin's house, Rahul lines up four pairs of slippers: blue, red, yellow, and green. The green pair is at the far right. The red pair is right next to green. The blue pair is not next to red. Which pair is at the far left?
options: a) Blue [answer] | b) Red | c) Yellow | d) Green

title: The Festival Mystery Bags
text:
At the colony festival celebration, Nikhil and Harsh stand before a game stall. Three gift bags—Blue, Orange, and Green—sit on the counter. Exactly one bag contains the prize token.

The tags read:
• Blue bag: "The token is not in this bag."
• Orange bag: "The token is not in the Green bag."
• Green bag: "The token is in this bag."

The stallkeeper smiles: "Only one tag tells the truth; the other two are false."

Which bag contains the token?
options: a) The Blue bag [answer] | b) The Orange bag | c) The Green bag | d) It is impossible to tell

title: Waiting in the Library
text: Aarav waited quietly in the school library while Sneha finished reading the comic book. He was being patient. What does patient mean?
options: a) Able to wait calmly [answer] | b) Speaking very loudly | c) Running very fast | d) Feeling very sleepy

title: Thoughtful at the wedding
text: At the family wedding, Diya saw that Anjali could not reach the snack table. Diya brought a plate over to share with her. Diya was being thoughtful. What does thoughtful mean?
options: a) Thinking about others' needs and helping [answer] | b) Being in a big hurry to finish first | c) Speaking loudly across the room | d) Forgetting what someone wanted

title: Staying Composed
text: While visiting his cousin Ishita, Aarav accidentally deleted her saved progress in their phone game. Ishita took a deep breath and stayed composed instead of shouting. What does composed mean here?
options: a) Calm and in control of her feelings [answer] | b) Loudly celebrating a big win | c) Confused about how the game works | d) Too anxious to say anything

title: Sister's Paper Castle
text: Thomas spent an hour helping his little sister Jaya rebuild her paper castle after it tore. Jaya felt grateful for his patience. Which word means the OPPOSITE of grateful?
options: a) Thankful | b) Ungrateful [answer] | c) Generous | d) Careful

title: Ayaan's Campaign Poster
text: At her cousin Ayaan's house, Ayaan excitedly unrolls a poster he spent all evening making for his school club election. The slogan is clever, but the lettering is cramped and hard to decipher. Meenakshi wants to help him, so she chooses to give a tactful response rather than blurting out her initial reaction. What does "tactful" mean here?
options: a) Carefully phrasing her thoughts so she is helpful without causing hurt [answer] | b) Praising the poster as flawless so Ayaan stays cheerful | c) Pointing out every flaw bluntly so the truth is immediately clear | d) Quickly changing the topic to avoid sharing any opinion at all

title: Finding Common Ground
text: During a heated debate prep in the classroom, Simran and Abdul disagreed sharply over their opening speech. Instead of arguing further, Abdul adopted a ______ tone, offering to blend Simran's ideas with his own to resolve the conflict. Which word best fits Abdul's approach?

text: You and Farhan agreed to take turns batting for ten balls each at the neighbourhood park. After finishing his turn, Farhan keeps holding the bat and announces, "I'm hitting so well today, I get another round!" It's your turn, and he gave his word. What do you do?
options: a) Snatch the bat from his hands and yell that he is a cheat | b) Look at him and say calmly, "We agreed on ten balls each, Farhan. It's my turn now." | c) Say nothing and quietly head back out to the boundary to field | d) Ask Uncle Thomas by the benches to help remind everyone of the rule

title: Next in Line
text: At football practice, you have been waiting in line for shooting drills. Just as your turn arrives, Vikram runs up and cuts ahead of you. What do you do?
options: a) Shout at Vikram and push him out of the way | b) Say calmly, 'Vikram, I was next. You can take the shot after me' | c) Say nothing and walk quietly to the back of the line | d) Tell Coach Thomas that Vikram jumped the line

title: The laptop turn
text: Abdul promised you could use the family laptop at five to finish an English assignment that closes at five-thirty. It is now five-fifteen, and he refuses to log off his multiplayer game, saying, "Chill out, just wait ten minutes." Your deadline is slipping away, and you feel furious. What do you do?
options: a) Slam the laptop lid shut and yell at him for breaking his word | b) Say nothing and try typing the long assignment on your phone screen | c) Tell him firmly, "You promised five. The portal closes at five-thirty, and I need the laptop now." | d) Ask Mum to step in so the agreed schedule is followed

title: Dada's Dinner Thali
text: At your cousin's wedding, your uncle asks you to help serve Dada his dinner. Just then, Gurpreet calls you over to join a big game of tag on the lawn with everyone. What do you do?
options: a) Tell Gurpreet to start, and say you will join as soon as Dada finishes | b) Ask Gurpreet to help you serve Dada so you both can play sooner | c) Run straight to the lawn before the game starts without you | d) Stay beside Dada, but grumble loudly so people know you are missing out

title: The Only Hoverboard
text: In an online game, you and Karthik unlock the only hoverboard on the island. Only one player can ride it. Karthik types, "Let me try!" You really want to ride it right now too. What do you do?
options: a) Quickly click to grab the board before Karthik can | b) Type, "You take the first turn, then pass it to me" | c) Let him take it without saying anything and feel glum

title: The Senior Drill
text: At football practice, Coach unexpectedly invites you and Joseph to join the senior squad's special tactical session. You've dreamed of this for months. But your phone buzzes: a reminder from Mum that Dadi needs you home by 5:30 p.m. to help her walk to the clinic while your parents finish work. Staying means breaking your promise at home; leaving means missing your big chance. What do you do?
options: a) Call Mum to explain the opportunity and ask if an aunt or neighbour can help Dadi today | b) Tell Coach and Joseph about your family commitment, leave on time, and ask Joseph to share drill notes later | c) Switch off my phone, stay for the full session, and make up an excuse later | d) Complain to Joseph that family duties always ruin your sports opportunities

title: The Kulfi Counter
text: At a family wedding reception, you wait patiently in a long line for kulfi. Just as you reach the front, Nikhil pushes right in front of you and reaches for a bowl. What do you do?
options: a) Shove his arm and shout, 'Get lost, I was here first!' | b) Look at him and say firmly, 'Nikhil, I waited my turn. Please go behind me.' | c) Say nothing and step back, letting him take your spot. | d) Tell the elder serving dessert, 'Excuse me, I was next in line.'

title: The Hidden Guide
text: During revision in the school library, Aarav nudges you with the only copy of the exam guide. 'Quick, slide it behind the old encyclopedias,' he whispers. 'If Section B gets it, their scores will beat ours.' He presses the book into your hands, waiting. What do you do?
options: a) Slip the book behind the encyclopedias like Aarav asks | b) Hand it back to Aarav and tell him firmly that hiding library books is wrong | c) Refuse to hide it, and suggest you both spend twenty minutes jotting down notes before returning it | d) Shrug, place the guide on a random table, and walk to the other side of the room

title: The broken party toy
text: At Aarav's birthday party, you accidentally step on his new toy car and the wheel snaps off. Nobody saw it happen. Aarav is in the other room cutting the cake. What do you do?
options: a) Hide the broken car behind the sofa and walk away | b) Tell Aarav what happened and offer to help fix it | c) Say Rahul was playing near the toys earlier

title: Balcony Confession
text: At Nandini's birthday party, Vikram pulls you out to the quiet balcony. He looks overwhelmed. "I've missed three weeks of coaching because I got completely lost in class, and now the teacher is calling home on Monday. I don't know what to do, but promise you won't tell anyone." You can tell this is far bigger than one bad day. What do you do?
options: a) Tell him to brush it off for now and come back inside to dance | b) Promise to keep his secret and help him invent an excuse | c) Encourage him to talk to a trusted adult, and offer to be there with him | d) Go tell his parents right away in the middle of the party

title: A secret at Kiran's house
text: At your cousin Kiran's house, Kiran is crying softly. For two weeks, older kids at the park have been cornering him and taking his pocket money. Kiran whispers, "Promise you won't tell Ma! They said it will get worse." What do you do?
options: a) Offer to go with Kiran to tell his mother together | b) Keep the secret and offer to face the older kids with him | c) Tell his mother immediately without telling Kiran first | d) Tell Kiran to simply stay inside the house from now on

title: Stage Credit
text: During the annual day drama rehearsal, Karthik steps up to the microphone and introduces the script you spent three evenings writing together as entirely his own work. The drama teacher praises his creativity, and Karthik smiles and accepts the credit without mentioning you. What do you do?
options: a) Interrupt loudly on stage and call Karthik a liar in front of the cast | b) Keep quiet and say nothing, but ignore Karthik for the rest of the day | c) Pull Karthik aside at the break and firmly tell him he needs to clarify your shared credit | d) Speak to the drama teacher privately after rehearsal with your shared draft notes

title: The Cracked Keepsake
text: At your cousin Pooja's house, you admire her sister Kiran's delicate ceramic project on the study table. While picking it up, it slips from your fingers and a corner chips off. Pooja is busy in the kitchen, and Kiran is returning from coaching in twenty minutes, already exhausted from exams. Nobody saw what happened, and Pooja might think the house cat knocked it down. What do you do?
options: a) Push the chip under the table and let everyone think the cat did it | b) Tell Pooja right away and wait together to explain honestly to Kiran, offering to help glue it | c) Try to stick it back with tape quietly so neither of them notices today | d) Leave the study room immediately and sit in the living room pretending to read

title: The last sparkler box
text: During the festival, Yash pushes past you and grabs the last sparkler box from the table. Your chest feels tight, your face burns, and your hands squeeze into tight fists. What do you do?
options: a) Shove Yash back and snatch the box out of his hand | b) Notice my tight fists, take three deep breaths to cool down, then ask to share | c) Pretend I don't care at all and look away | d) Shout loudly so all the neighbors stare at him

title: Baton Drop
text: During relay practice on the school ground, you fumble the baton pass to Ishita, and it drops into the mud. Your team finishes last in the trial heat. Your chest tightens, and a thought pops up: "I ruin everything for our team." What do you do?
options: a) Tell myself I'm hopeless at running and sit out the rest of practice | b) Crack a loud joke about greasy fingers so no one notices how upset I am | c) Remind myself that one mistake doesn't define me, and ask Ishita to drill the pass again | d) Complain that Ishita ran too fast so the coach doesn't blame me

title: Cancelled zoo trip
text: In the class group chat, Aarav posts that tomorrow's zoo trip is cancelled due to heavy rain. You had packed your favourite snacks and felt excited all week. You feel crushed and annoyed. What do you do?
options: a) Take a slow breath and remind myself that the trip will still happen on a sunny day | b) Mute the group chat angrily, kick your backpack, and sulk in your room | c) Text Aarav in the chat to see if a few friends want to play online ludo instead

title: The Missed Shield
text: During a clutch online match, your squad loses because you mistimed your shield. Ravi sighs heavily into his headset, and an unhelpful thought instantly hits you: "I ruin every match, they only play with me out of pity." Vikram quickly types into the lobby, "Ready up, let's go again." You want to quit to spare them, but leaving mid-session gives the team an automatic rank penalty. What do you do?
options: a) Disconnect right away so they don't have to carry me through another match | b) Remind myself that one bad play doesn't make me useless, and ask how to adjust our timing | c) Type in the chat that my network lagged so neither of them blames me | d) Stay in the game but mute my mic and play overly safe so I don't mess up again

title: The New Comic on the Desk
text: The librarian puts a brand-new comic on the desk. She asks you and Aarav to wait five minutes without touching it while she gets the ink stamp. The bright cover is right in front of you, and you really want to peek inside. What do you do?
options: a) Open the comic quickly and flip through the first pages | b) Turn toward the shelf and look at the riddle books while waiting | c) Peek inside, crease the corner by mistake, and admit it as soon as she returns | d) Sit on your hands and count backward from sixty to keep still

title: The Skipping Rope
text: You are learning to skip rope in the park with Sana. You trip four times in a row. A thought pops up: "I'm just clumsy, I can never do this." Sana holds out the rope for another go. What do you do?
options: a) Remind myself that tripping happens when learning, and try again | b) Tell Sana I need to watch her rhythm first, since new skills take time | c) Say my knee hurts so I can sit down and stop missing | d) Drop the rope and decide skipping is a silly game anyway

title: Sidelined at the party
text: At Gurpreet's birthday party, everyone forms pairs for a gaming tournament. The brackets fill up quickly, and you are left without a partner for the first round. You spent all week looking forward to competing. Now Karthik and the others are gathered around the screen shouting with excitement, while you are left on the sidelines. What do you do?
options: a) Pull up a chair beside Karthik to scout opponent tactics and cheer for his team | b) Sit alone in the dining room staring at the wall until someone asks what happened | c) Accept missing this round, grab some samosas, and start a board game at the side table | d) Complain to Gurpreet that the bracket was unfair and demand they restart it

title: The Mock Test Score
text: During evening tuition, Sir returns our mock tests. Irfan, who studied with me all week, leans over and loudly points at my low score: "Wait, didn't you say you understood this chapter?" My cheeks burn hot, my fingernails dig into my palms, and my chest feels tight and breathless. Yash turns around to stare, and Sir pauses mid-lecture. What do you do?
options: a) Snap back loudly that Irfan barely passed his own paper | b) Notice my clenched hands, take two slow breaths to steady myself, and tell Irfan quietly we will talk after class | c) Shove the paper into my bag and ignore everyone, pretending nothing happened | d) Complain to Sir right away that Irfan is mocking my marks

title: Unpinned in the chat
text: You spent an hour compiling revision notes for tomorrow's test and pinned them in the class group chat. Two minutes later, Farhan removes the pin and posts a random meme instead. A few classmates react with laughing emojis. Your face burns, and your fingers hover over the keyboard, ready to fire back. What do you do?
options: a) Fire off a sarcastic message in the group calling Farhan childish | b) Message Farhan privately to ask why he unpinned my notes | c) Take a breath, put the phone down for five minutes, and quietly re-pin the notes later

title: Rain at the Reception
text: At a cousin's wedding, heavy rain stops you and Farhan from playing outside. Uncle says everyone must stay inside the noisy hall. You feel restless and disappointed. What do you do?
options: a) Sit in a corner with crossed arms and ignore everyone | b) Ask Farhan to find toothpicks so you two can build small puzzles at a table | c) Remind myself that rain happens, and suggest checking out the dessert counter

title: The Library Comic
text: In the library, you reach for the last space comic. Vikram quickly snatches it right from your fingers. Your fists squeeze tight, your teeth clench, and your chest feels suddenly hot. Vikram sits down at a table to read. What do you do?
options: a) Squeeze my fists harder and snatch the comic right off his table | b) Notice my tight hands, uncurl my fingers, breathe out, and ask Vikram to share the desk | c) Notice my hot chest, take a slow breath, and quietly ask the librarian to set turns | d) Swallow the feeling down, walk to another shelf, and pretend I do not care

title: Board Problem
text: During evening tuition, sir writes a complex trigonometry problem on the board. Divya finishes hers in five minutes, but your page is full of scribbles. Frustrated, a heavy thought takes over: "I'll never get this, my brain just isn't built for maths." Sir announces that everyone must show their working in ten minutes. What do you do?
options: a) Remind myself it's just a new topic, and ask Divya which formula she used for step two | b) Decide I'm just hopeless at trigonometry and quickly copy Divya's page so sir doesn't scold me | c) Accept that I need time, take a steady breath, and work through the first step alone at my pace | d) Shove my notebook into my bag and claim my pen ran out to avoid the pressure

title: The Fellowship Email
text: The email arrives: you got selected for the month-long summer science camp in Bengaluru. Yash high-fives you, grinning ear-to-ear, while Ma dials Dadi to celebrate. You feel a burst of pride, but looking around your room, a sudden anxious knot tightens in your stomach about being away from home alone. Yash asks, "Aren't you totally thrilled?" What do you do?
options: a) Tell Yash I am really excited about the camp, but also a bit nervous about leaving home | b) Pretend I only feel pure excitement and start bragging about the campus | c) Shrug and say the camp probably won't even be that interesting | d) Slip away to my room and search online for reasons to cancel my spot

title: The Spice Stall Run
text: At the busy market, Papa hands Yash twenty rupees. "Go ahead to the spice stall alone and buy turmeric," Papa says. Yash feels big and excited, but also a little nervous about the bustling crowd. Papa smiles and asks, "Ready?" What do you do?
options: a) Tell Papa I am excited to try, but a bit nervous too | b) Boast that I am totally brave and dash ahead into the crowd | c) Pretend I don't care and tell Papa to buy it himself | d) Nod quietly and drag my feet, hiding the tight feeling in my chest

title: Counting the Market Change
text: At the vegetable market, your mother Meenakshi asks you to count the change. You get the total wrong twice. You think, "I'm just terrible at maths." Meenakshi is waiting with the cloth bags. What do you do?
options: a) Tell myself I am still learning, take a breath, and recount | b) Believe I will never get it right and hand the coins back | c) Guess a number quickly so the vendor doesn't stare

title: Meme in the Class Chat
text: In the class group chat, Abdul posts a meme teasing your science poster. Suddenly, your cheeks feel burning hot and your fingers squeeze the phone tightly. What do you do?
options: a) Notice my burning face and tight hands, put the phone down, and breathe slowly | b) Type an angry reply straight away while my fingers are shaking | c) Post a laughing emoji to push the heat down and pretend it is funny | d) Step away from the screen and show the message to my mother

title: The Library Envelope
text: In a quiet corner of the school library, the teacher hands you an envelope. Your essay won the state competition, earning a trip to Delhi. But Sana, who researched beside you every evening, didn't make the shortlist. Looking down, your heart leaps with excitement, yet a heavy pang of sadness for her hits at the exact same moment. Sana looks up from her notebook, waiting to know what the letter says. What do you do?
options: a) Show Sana the certificate and talk only about Delhi, pushing away the guilt you feel. | b) Tell Sana you won, sharing both how thrilled you are and how sad you feel that she missed out. | c) Hide the envelope and pretend the results were delayed so she does not feel low. | d) Tell her you won, but insist the contest was pointless and you do not care about going.

title: Voice Note in the Park
text: At the neighbourhood park bench, Irfan plays a voice note from Mary laughing about how your voice cracked during the class presentation. Instantly, your face burns, your heart hammers against your ribs, and your hands squeeze into tight, shaking balls. Irfan looks up, waiting to see what you will do. What do you do?
options: a) Notice my pounding chest and clenched fists, take three slow breaths, and wait for the heat to cool | b) Tell Irfan right now that the voice note is mean and ask him to switch it off | c) Fire off a sarcastic reply in the group chat pointing out a mistake Mary made | d) Force a laugh and pretend it is funny, keeping my clenched hands tucked in my pockets

title: The Assembly Quiz
text: Teacher announces you will lead the school assembly quiz tomorrow. You feel proud and thrilled, but your tummy twists with worry about making mistakes on the mic. Aarav turns around and asks, "Aren't you totally excited?" What do you do?
options: a) Tell Aarav I am really excited, but also nervous about the big mic | b) Say, "Yes, completely!" and try to ignore the nervous flutter inside | c) Tell Aarav I feel nervous, keeping my happy feeling hidden so I do not brag | d) Shrug and say it is no big deal so Aarav thinks I am fearless

title: Missed Catches
text: During recess on the playground, you drop the ball twice. Shreya calls for the next round. A thought pops into your head: "I ruin every game." What do you do?
options: a) Believe the thought, sit on the bench alone, and give up | b) Remind myself it was only two drops and join the next throw | c) Pretend my shoe hurts so Shreya does not see me miss again

title: The Maths Test Return
text: In tuition class, Meenakshi ma'am gives back the maths tests. You scored full marks, but your benchmate Yash got a red cross on almost every sum. Meenakshi ma'am smiles and asks how you feel about your test. What do you do?
options: a) Cheer loudly and wave my paper around the table | b) Say I feel happy about my score, but also a bit sad for Yash | c) Shrug and pretend I do not care at all about marks | d) Stuff the test paper into my bag and look away

title: Campfire banter
text: During the class trip around the campfire, Thomas mimics the clumsy way you climbed the hill today. Everyone bursts out laughing. Your ears burn red, your jaw locks tight, and your fingernails dig deep into your palms. What do you do?
options: a) Notice my clenched hands and take a slow breath before saying anything | b) Snap back immediately and mock the way Thomas dropped his mess tray | c) Force an uncomfortable laugh and swallow the tight lump in my throat | d) Storm away from the circle into the dark tents

title: Waiting at the Nets
text: Coach asks Aarav to bat first today. You feel sad waiting on the bench. What do you do?
options: a) Ask Coach if I can field now | b) Cheer loudly for Aarav's big hits | c) Cross my arms and look away

title: The Sunny Line
text: We must stay in line on our trip. Imran feels very dizzy in the sun. What do you do?
options: a) Stay in line so teacher is happy | b) Call the teacher to help Imran | c) Tell Imran to just keep walking

title: Rain at Home
text: It starts raining outside. You cheer because you love rain. Simran cries because she wanted the park. What do you do?
options: a) Jump and shout, 'Rain is the best!' | b) Ask Simran what she wants to play | c) Say, 'Do not cry, rain is good!'

title: Line for the Deer
text: You wait in line to see the deer on the school trip. Noor pushes in front of you, and you feel upset. What do you do?
options: a) Push her back and shout at her. | b) Say calmly, "I was first, please go behind." | c) Look down and say nothing at all.

title: No lights at home
text: The power goes out at home. You and Siddharth feel hot and bored. What do you do?
options: a) Open the window for some cool air | b) Make shadow birds on the wall with Siddharth | c) Cross your arms and sulk in bed

title: Wet shoes on the bus
text: Rahul drops his water bottle on your shoes. Your tummy feels tight and your teeth clamp shut. What do you do?
options: a) Kick Rahul's bag under the seat | b) Breathe slowly to relax your tummy | c) Hold it in and stay quiet

title: Rain on the bus trip
text: Rain stops your school trip games. You feel sad because you cannot run with Imran. What do you do?
options: a) Ask Imran to play games inside | b) Watch the cool rain make puddles | c) Cross your arms and sulk alone

title: Shadows in the Dark
text: The lights go out at home. Bhavna tells Harsh he cannot play shadows. Harsh sits alone and looks sad. What do you do?
options: a) Tell Bhavna, "Harsh can play with us." | b) Play only with Bhavna | c) Ask Papa to help us share

title: Balloon Tag
text: Children play balloon tag at the party. Chirag walks slowly and stands alone. What do you do?
options: a) Say, "Chirag can play with me!" | b) Run off to play without him | c) Tell an aunty Chirag is left out

title: The Big Animal Book
text: There is only one big animal book. You and Harsh both pull it. What do you do?
options: a) Say, "Let us read it together!" | b) Yank it hard and keep it | c) Let go sadly and walk away

title: The Spilled Sweet
text: Aarav drops his sweet at the wedding. He smiles big, but his chin shakes. What do you do?
options: a) Smile back and say, 'It is funny!' | b) Say, 'I feel sad too. Are you?' | c) Walk away to find more sweets

title: The Dropped Bells
text: Simran drops her bells at rehearsal. She laughs loudly, but her chin is wobbling. What do you do?
options: a) Say, "I feel nervous on stage too." | b) Laugh with her at the loud noise | c) Say, "Hurry and pick them up!"

title: Stuck on the Tent Pole
text: You are at a wedding with Imran. Imran is stuck high on the tent pole and crying. What do you do?
options: a) Go find an adult to help | b) Climb up to pull him down | c) Tell him to jump down alone

title: Wet Notebook
text: You spill water on Farhan's tuition notebook. Nobody saw you do it. What do you do?
options: a) Tell Farhan and help dry the pages | b) Push the book back under his bag | c) Say that Abdul spilled the water

title: The Bumpy Ball
text: It is football practice, and Aarav gets the new ball. You must use the bumpy old ball. What do you do?
options: a) Sit down and do not play | b) Ask Aarav to take turns kicking | c) See how high the old ball bounces

title: Quiet Line at the Zoo
text: You must stay quiet in line. Yash trips and hurts his knee. What do you do?
options: a) Call the teacher to help Yash | b) Stay quiet and keep walking in line | c) Tell Yash, "Shh, no talking!"

title: The Library Book Drop
text: In the library, Manav drops his book. He laughs, but his eyes look wet. What do you do?
options: a) Laugh along with Manav's joke. | b) Say, "I feel bad when I drop things." | c) Pick up the book for him.

title: Football or Races
text: Coach says we will play football today. You cheer, but Chirag frowns because he wanted running races. What do you do?
options: a) Jump and shout, "Football is the best!" | b) Ask Chirag, "Did you want to race?" | c) Tell Chirag to stop making faces.

title: Quiet Time at Home
text: Papa says, "Stay very quiet now." Little Gopal bumps his knee and cries. What do you do?
options: a) Whisper to Papa that Gopal is hurt | b) Shush Gopal so he stays quiet | c) Sit still and cover my ears

title: The Scooter Turn
text: You wait for Arnav's scooter. Arnav rides it again and skips your turn. What do you do?
options: a) Say, "Arnav, it is my turn now." | b) Push Arnav off the scooter | c) Sit down quietly and say nothing

title: The Only Green Crayon
text: Tuition has art time today. Jaya takes the only green crayon. What do you do?
options: a) Ask Jaya to share the green crayon. | b) Use yellow and make a bright tree. | c) Push my book away and stop.

title: Stars on the Desk
text: Noor Ma'am puts shiny stars on your desk. She says, "Wait until craft time." What do you do?
options: a) Cover the stars with my notebook | b) Stick one on my hand right now | c) Ask Noor Ma'am to keep them safe

title: The Lost Key
text: Joseph is crying by his desk. He cannot find his house key anywhere. What do you do?
options: a) Take Joseph to tell the teacher | b) Tell Joseph to keep it secret | c) Say, "Do not worry about it!"
